note.en: What you see: With the probe on the left flank, the spleen appears as a smaller crescent with the left kidney below and the bright diaphragm above. The splenorenal recess between them is the dependent pocket on this side, and the stomach bubble may flash nearby with shifting gas shadows. In health spleen and kidney touch with no dark stripe between them. This window is harder than the right side because ribs and stomach gas break up the image, so patience with positioning matters more here.

label.en: Spleen, left kidney, splenorenal recess between them, diaphragm above the spleen

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Spleen, left kidney, splenorenal recess between them, diaphragm above the spleen.

Landmarks to confirm: Spleen, left kidney, splenorenal recess between them, diaphragm above the spleen.

Common mistakes and correction: Stomach bubble mimicking fluid around the spleen: watch for shifting gas and confirm the stripe persists across breaths. Rib shadow hiding the recess: move one space and angle between ribs. Too posterior a plane that loses the diaphragm: tilt forward until the bright curve returns.

Normal values with units: No numeric threshold applies. In health no anechoic stripe separates spleen and kidney. Any persistent dark stripe in the splenorenal recess after trauma is abnormal and needs urgent senior review.

Pitfalls: This is the most commonly missed FAST window, so never skip it when the right side looks clear. Fluid here may track late, so repeat the view in an unstable patient. Record when gas or ribs limit the view so the team knows the examination was incomplete.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Place the probe in the left posterior axillary line between the eighth and eleventh ribs with the marker toward the head. Angle coronal and oblique until spleen, kidney and diaphragm show together. Slide back rather than forward since the spleen sits posterior. Fan slowly through the recess and glance above the diaphragm for chest fluid. If the stomach bubble fills the screen, ask the patient to breathe quietly and retry between breaths.

q.en: Where does the probe sit for the left upper quadrant view?

o.en: Midclavicular line low on the belly
Posterior axillary line between the eighth and eleventh ribs

why.en: The spleen sits posterior, so the posterior axillary line in the lower rib spaces is the window.

q.en: A dark pocket flashes near the spleen with gas shadows. What is correct?

o.en: Press harder to squash the bubble
Confirm the stripe persists across breaths and is not shifting gas

why.en: Stomach gas mimics fluid, so confirm a persistent stripe across breaths before calling it positive.

q.en: Why does guidance stress completing this window?

o.en: Never skip it even when the right side looks clear
Skip it when the right side is clear

why.en: This is the most commonly missed FAST window, so skipping it leaves trauma assessment incomplete.
